fields.description:
`bridge preview` replaces `--mode reconcile-check` and `--mode dry-run`. A design spike established
these are NOT a shared intermediate — they share only `fetcher.compute_snapshot`, the binding store,
and the `classify` module, and diverge on everything downstream:

- Local set: reconcile-check reads every `.cache.json` dir including archived/deleted; dry-run runs
  `rebar list --full` (active only).
- Field comparison: reconcile-check uses `_compare_pair`, UNARBITRATED — any difference is a
  discrepancy. Dry-run uses `outbound_field_diff`, arbitrated against the per-binding baseline
  (ADR 0026) with directionality suppression and local-wins.
- Neither output is derivable from the other. A reconcile-check discrepancy can produce NO mutation
  (baseline says local is unchanged); a dry-run mutation can exist with NO discrepancy (ADOPT of an
  unbound issue, TERMINAL_TRANSITION for an archived ticket — both invisible to the bound-pair loop).

`_compare_pair` is the differ's comparison re-implemented by hand, and its own comments prove it is
chasing the original: "must match the differ's exclusion set exactly", "canonicalized the same way
625b canonicalized the outbound differ". It already imports `_assignee_matches` from the differ.

Recommendation: ONE verb, ONE pass, two sections — `{plan, drift}` — because two verbs would run the
expensive Jira fetch twice. But the merge is real work, not a rename: the field detail must come
from the differ (surface `outbound_field_diff`'s existing `changed` dict on the plan entry) and
`_compare_pair` must be DELETED, or you have shipped two computations behind one verb.

**Also: preview must take no lock.** Today `dry-run` runs the full lock ceremony including
`_purge_committed_reconciler_locks` (a git CAS commit) and can STEAL A LIVE PASS'S LEASE to run a
read-only preview.

**Two bugs folded in.** `docs/user-guide.md:364` documents `rebar reconcile --dry-run`, which does
not exist — argparse's `allow_abbrev` resolves it to `--dry-run-enumerate`, so it prints ticket
directory paths and exits 0 WITHOUT reconciling, looking exactly like a successful dry run.
Reproduced. Setting `allow_abbrev=False` makes that whole error class impossible rather than fixing
one instance; a verb (not a flag) makes it unforgettable.

This ticket gates nothing else in the epic and can land independently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge preview` runs one cap-0 pass and emits both the plan and the field-level drift
- [ ] Field detail comes from the differ; `reconcile_check._compare_pair` is deleted
- [ ] Preview acquires no lock and never purges or steals one
- [ ] The two local-ticket loaders are reconciled to one read
- [ ] `allow_abbrev=False` on the parser, with a test that an abbreviated/unknown option exits 2
- [ ] `docs/user-guide.md:364` is corrected
- [ ] The `bridge_state/reconcile-check.json` write is dropped; preview writes stdout
- [ ] `preview` and `sync` emit the SAME manifest shape, including `live` — the render split
      (`render_throttle` vs `render_dry_run_or_strict`, `apply_planning.py:189-195`) collapses to one
      renderer and the no-manifest-in-LIVE contract is retired
- [ ] A test asserts a `live` run emits a manifest carrying the applied/failed tally, pinning the
      `c903-42b9-0f17-45cc` regression closed by construction rather than by the salvage read at
      `apply_planning.py:154-187`
- [ ] A test asserts a `preview` manifest and a `sync` manifest for the same store are
      field-comparable, so "preview then sync" can be diffed
